name: Tamsulosin + Deflazacort
meta: Tamsulosin Hydrochloride: Selective alpha-1A/1D adrenoceptor antagonist; Deflazacort: Glucocorticoid (oxazoline derivative of prednisolone)
Schedule H – prescription only; Deflazacort: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), sparingly soluble in water.
White to off-white crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.

Tamsulosin Hydrochloride: Generic in the USA since 2010; widely used for medical expulsive therapy of distal ureteric stones. First approval/introduction: Japan 1993 (Yamanouchi, now Astellas); US 1997 (Boehringer Ingelheim). Deflazacort: An oxazoline derivative of prednisolone; potency is about 70–90% that of prednisone (6–7.5 mg deflazacort ≈ 5 mg prednisolone). First approval/introduction: Patented 1969; approved 1985 (Lepetit / Gruppo Lepetit, Italy); US FDA 2017 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Tamsulosin relaxes distal ureteric smooth muscle; the corticosteroid reduces ureteric mucosal oedema and inflammation at the stone site – together improving stone passage rate and time.

Tamsulosin Hydrochloride Blocks alpha-1A and alpha-1D receptors in prostatic, bladder-neck and distal ureteric smooth muscle, improving urinary flow in BPH and facilitating passage of distal ureteric stones. Receptor / target profile: Selective antagonist at alpha-1A and alpha-1D receptors in prostate, bladder neck and ureter.

Deflazacort Inactive prodrug converted to 21-desacetyl deflazacort; binds glucocorticoid receptors to suppress inflammatory gene transcription and immune responses. 6–7.5 mg deflazacort ≈ 5 mg prednisolone; reported to have relatively less effect on bone and glucose metabolism. Receptor / target profile: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist reducing inflammatory gene transcription and immune activity.
Summary: Modified release; bioavailability ~100% fasting; Tmax 4–5 h (6–7 h fed). ~99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Half-life 9–15 h.
Plasma esterases to active 21-desacetyl deflazacort; then CYP3A4
Summary: Rapidly absorbed and converted to active metabolite; Tmax 1–2 h. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life ~1.1–1.9 h (biological effect longer).

Tamsulosin Hydrochloride: Hypotension; supportive care. Deflazacort: Acute overdose rarely serious; chronic excess causes Cushingoid effects. Supportive care.
Dellabella et al., J Urol 2005 – tamsulosin plus deflazacort increased expulsion rate and reduced expulsion time of distal ureteric stones.
